claims.text: The target material consists of W particles or connected W regions embedded in a Cu matrix.
Conventional W–Cu powder-metallurgy routes tend to produce interfacial defects, voids, and phase inhomogeneity because of the large W–Cu melting-temperature gap.
A thin, conformal Cu coating can be deposited on W particles by chemical vapor deposition before consolidation.
Pre-coating W particles with Cu will enhance W–Cu interfacial bonding.
Pre-coating W particles with Cu will improve Cu wetting during sintering.
The Cu pre-coating will reduce void formation in the consolidated W–Cu composite.
The Cu pre-coating will reduce phase-separated regions in the consolidated W–Cu composite.
Spark-plasma sintering is applicable to consolidation of powders intended for high-temperature or plasma-facing service.
The conformal Cu layer will enhance atomic interdiffusion between W and Cu.
Enhanced interdiffusion will promote nearly perfect contact between W and Cu.
Depositing a thin, uniform Cu layer on W lowers the W–Cu interfacial energy.
Lower interfacial energy and improved wetting produce a more uniform diffusion-bonded W–Cu microstructure with fewer voids.
A more uniform, low-void W–Cu microstructure will provide more efficient thermal transport.
The coated composite will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise identical SPS composite made with uncoated W particles.
The coated composite will have higher hardness or strength than an otherwise identical uncoated-particle composite.
The coated composite will better resist irradiation-induced embrittlement than an otherwise identical uncoated-particle composite.
Fusion-reactor divertor materials and joints must operate under high thermal flux and irradiation exposure.
The intervention may lose effectiveness if a uniform CVD coating cannot be maintained over complex W geometries.
Direct casting, mechanical alloying, and SPS of uncoated W particles typically suffer from voids, phase inhomogeneity, or limited W–Cu interfacial contact.
The proposed controlled experiment compares coated and uncoated W particles consolidated by SPS under otherwise identical conditions.
